title: TRACE: Learning to Self-Calibrate Wireless Digital Twins from ISAC Measurements
abstract: arXiv:2609.32923v2 Announce Type: replace  Abstract: Wireless digital twins (DTs) rely on 3D environment models to predict radio propagation and support wireless-network decisions, yet these models are often initialized from imperfect 3D maps. Errors in building position, height, footprint, and orientation can therefore cause a high-fidelity propagation engine to simulate the wrong physical environment. In this paper, we study how a deployed wireless network can repair an existing DT using its own radio frequency (RF) measurements. In particular, we introduce Twin Residual Alignment and Calibration Engine (TRACE), a physics-grounded learning-based self-calibration framework that treats twin maintenance as residual alignment between the physical world and the current DT. translated_title: TRACE：从ISAC测量中学习自校准无线数字孪生
translated_abstract: 无线数字孪生（DT）依赖三维环境模型来预测无线电传播并支持无线网络决策，然而这些模型通常基于不完美的三维地图进行初始化。因此，建筑物位置、高度、底面轮廓和朝向的误差可能导致高保真传播引擎模拟出错误的物理环境。本文研究了已部署的无线网络如何利用自身的射频（RF）测量来修复现有的数字孪生。特别地，我们提出了孪生残差对齐与校准引擎（TRACE），这是一个基于物理的学习型自校准框架，将孪生维护视为物理世界与当前数字孪生之间的残差对齐问题。TRACE使用与物理测量相同的感知配置对当前数字孪生进行光线追踪，将测量和仿真得到的射频信号相干地反投影到统一的世界网格上，并提取相同的局部区域……
tldr: 该论文提出TRACE框架，通过将实测与仿真的ISAC射频信号相干反投影到统一世界网格进行残差对齐，使已部署的无线网络能够利用自身测量数据自校准并修复因三维地图误差而失准的数字孪生。
en_tdlr: TRACE is a physics-grounded learning framework that self-calibrates wireless digital twins by coherently backprojecting measured and simulated RF signals onto a common world grid for residual alignment, enabling deployed networks to repair DTs corrupted by imperfect 3D maps using their own ISAC measurements.
